meta.description: Direction and spatial-position vocabulary — compass directions, relative position nouns, range/comparison words built on 以, and the extra vocabulary needed to give or follow directions.
meta.note: Most of these are plain nouns and don't conjugate, so this is a browsable reference rather than a conjugation drill set. 曲がる (magaru, “to turn”) and 渡る (wataru, “to cross”) already exist as full conjugating entries in your Word Library — they're cross-referenced here rather than duplicated.

categories.position: Relative position nouns — always paired with の (e.g. 本の上 'on top of the book')
categories.range: 以-prefixed words marking a boundary or range relative to a reference point
categories.directions-vocab: Extra vocabulary for giving or asking for directions

words.usage_note: Compass words combine directly with の to modify a noun (東の窓 'the east-facing window') or with に/へ for direction of movement (東に進む 'proceed eastward').

examples.jp: 太陽は東から出る。
examples.en: The sun rises in the east.

examples.jp: 太陽は西に沈む。
examples.en: The sun sets in the west.

examples.jp: 南の島へ旅行する。
examples.en: I travel to an island in the south.

examples.jp: 北の地域は寒い。
examples.en: The northern region is cold.

words.usage_note: Intercardinal directions in Japanese are built north/south-first: 北東 (northeast), not 東北. This is the reverse order from some other conventions, so it's worth memorizing as fixed compounds.

examples.jp: 風が北東から吹いている。
examples.en: The wind is blowing from the northeast.

examples.jp: 北西の空が晩ってきた。
examples.en: The sky to the northwest has clouded over.

examples.jp: 南東アジアを旅行する。
examples.en: I travel around Southeast Asia.

examples.jp: 南西の空が明るい。
examples.en: The sky to the southwest is bright.

words.meaning_en: above; on top of; the top
words.usage_note: Position nouns like this attach to another noun with の: 機の上に本がある 'there is a book on the desk'. Don't confuse with 上げる (ageru, 'to raise' — a different, verb, word).

examples.jp: 機の上に本がある。
examples.en: There is a book on top of the desk.

words.usage_note: Also read もと in some fixed expressions (法のもと 'under the law'), but した is the everyday spatial reading.

examples.jp: 機の下に猫がいる。
examples.en: There is a cat under the desk.

words.usage_note: Doubles as a time word: 食事の前 'before the meal'.

examples.jp: 駅の前で待つ。
examples.en: I'll wait in front of the station.

words.usage_note: Spatial only — for 'after' in time, use 後 (あと) instead.

examples.jp: 学校の後ろに公園がある。
examples.en: There is a park behind the school.

examples.jp: 左に曲がる。
examples.en: I turn left.

examples.jp: 右に曲がる。
examples.en: I turn right.

words.usage_note: Also used abstractly for 'among/within a group': 三人の中で一番背が高い 'the tallest among the three'.

examples.jp: カバンの中に財布がある。
examples.en: There is a wallet inside the bag.

examples.jp: 外で待っている。
examples.en: I'm waiting outside.

words.usage_note: For things of the same kind lined up (houses, seats, buildings); compare そば/近く for general nearness regardless of category.

examples.jp: 銀行の隣にカフェがある。
examples.en: There is a cafe next to the bank.

examples.jp: 道の向かいに郵便局がある。
examples.en: There is a post office across the street.

words.usage_note: Emphasizes closeness/proximity to a person or thing, often with a sense of accompaniment; 近く is more neutrally about physical distance.

examples.jp: 駅のそばに住んでいる。
examples.en: I live near the station.

examples.jp: この近くにコンビニはありますか。
examples.en: Is there a convenience store near here?

examples.jp: 遠くに山が見える。
examples.en: I can see mountains in the distance.

words.usage_note: Spatial ('between two things': 木と木の間) and temporal ('during/while': 夏休みの間) uses are both common.

examples.jp: 学校と駅の間に公園がある。
examples.en: There is a park between the school and the station.

words.meaning_en: corner (of a street or building, outside edge)
words.usage_note: The outside corner of a building or intersection — the one you'd turn at. Compare 隅 for an inside nook or corner of a room.

examples.jp: あの角を曲がってください。
examples.en: Please turn at that corner.

words.meaning_en: corner; nook (of a room or enclosed space)
words.usage_note: The inside corner of a room or box, unlike 角 which is an outside corner you'd walk around.

examples.jp: 部屋の隅に本棚がある。
examples.en: There is a bookshelf in the corner of the room.

words.usage_note: Attaches to a number or noun to mean 'that amount or more': 二十歳以上 'twenty years old or older'. As a standalone noun in writing, 以上 also closes off a list or statement ('the above / that is all').

examples.jp: 二十歳以上の人だけ入れる。
examples.en: Only people twenty years old or older may enter.

words.usage_note: Mirror image of 以上: 十歳以下 'ten years old or younger'. In documents, 以下同様 means 'the same applies below/hereafter'.

examples.jp: 十歳以下の子供は無料です。
examples.en: Children ten years old or younger are free.

words.usage_note: Sets an upper boundary that is not exceeded: 一時間以内 'within one hour'.

examples.jp: 一時間以内に戻ってください。
examples.en: Please come back within one hour.

words.usage_note: Not to be confused with 意外 (igai, “surprising, unexpected”) — same reading, completely different word and kanji.

examples.jp: 日曜日以外は開いている。
examples.en: It's open every day except Sunday.

words.usage_note: Marks a time boundary looking backward: 三時以前 'before three o'clock'. Compare 前 (mae), which is more general/relative.

examples.jp: 三時以前に来てください。
examples.en: Please come before three o'clock.

words.meaning_en: after (a point in time); from now on
words.usage_note: Mirror of 以前: marks a time boundary looking forward. 今後 (kongo) is a common near-synonym meaning specifically 'from now on'.

examples.jp: 三時以後におこしください。
examples.en: Please come after three o'clock.

words.meaning_en: since (a point in the past, continuing to now)
words.usage_note: Unlike 以後 (which just marks 'after X'), 以来 specifically frames an unbroken continuation from that point to the present: 卒業以来会っていない 'haven't met since graduating'.

examples.jp: 卒業以来会っていない。
examples.en: I haven't met them since graduating.

words.usage_note: Functions as a な-adjective/adverb: まっすぐな道 'a straight road', まっすぐ行く 'go straight'. The single most common word in giving directions.

examples.jp: この道をまっすぐ行ってください。
examples.en: Please go straight down this road.

words.meaning_en: to turn (at a corner or intersection)
words.usage_note: Already in your Word Library as a full conjugating verb (godan) — look it up there for the complete conjugation table.

examples.jp: 次の角を左に曲がる。
examples.en: Turn left at the next corner.

words.usage_note: Already in your Word Library as a full conjugating verb (godan) — look it up there for the complete conjugation table.

examples.jp: 橋を渡ると公園がある。
examples.en: Cross the bridge and there's a park.

words.meaning_en: the end of a street or corridor (where it dead-ends into something)
words.usage_note: Marks where a straight path terminates: 突き当たりを右に曲がる 'turn right at the end (of this street)'.

examples.jp: 突き当たりを右に曲がってください。
examples.en: Turn right at the end of the street.

examples.jp: 次の信号を左に曲がってください。
examples.en: Turn left at the next traffic light.

examples.jp: あの交差点を渡ってください。
examples.en: Please cross that intersection.

examples.jp: あの高いビルが目印です。
examples.en: That tall building is the landmark.
